advice:
GOAL: replace the "rectangle + one trailer row + fixed 400x200x6 ft pond" with a parametric layout whose outputs land inside local comp ranges. Draw the building, every paved element and the open space so that impervious %, coverage and counts come from geometry, not assumptions.

1) PICK A CONFIGURATION FROM USABLE DEPTH
Usable depth D is the shorter dimension of the net developable polygon after setbacks, stream buffers (Union City/Palmetto: 50 ft undisturbed + 25 ft impervious setback = 75 ft; South Fulton: 100 ft), floodplain/wetlands and residential buffers.

Rear-load / front-load (single-loaded) needs:
D_min = front yard + car bay (62 ft double-loaded, 9x18 stalls on a 24-26 ft aisle) + W + truck court C + trailer row T + rear yard.
- W = 180-320 ft. Comps: 300 ft Southpark, 310 ft Hillwood; operator prototype 260.
- C = 130-185 ft. 130 is the floor (60 ft apron + 70-75 ft maneuvering, ARC: 60 + 75 = 135); 185 is current Class A.
- T = 55 ft (trailer-only stall; tractor-trailer stall is 80 ft).
- Typical D_min is about 520-720 ft.

Cross-dock needs:
D_min = yard + T + C + W + C + T + yard.
- W = 400-620 ft (400 at Prologis 1525 Oakley, 470 Hillwood, 520 prototype; Cushman says 500-660 is optimal).
- Typical D_min is about 1,000-1,250 ft.

Rules:
- Use cross-dock only when the target is at least about 300k SF and the D threshold is met.
- Otherwise use single-loaded, with docks facing away from the public frontage (ARC: loading interior, not facing roads).
- For shallow, wide parcels, run the long axis parallel to the frontage.
- Length/width aspect 2:1 to 4:1. Comps: 1,392x400 = 3.5; 1,407x300 = 4.7.

2) SIZE THE BUILDING FROM SF
Footprint = SF / (1 - mezzanine share); office is 1-3% inside the footprint (Prologis 1.6% in 3 corner pods).

Typical net land need, building + courts + trailers + cars + drives + about 10% detention, from geometry checked against comps:

| Building | Typical form | Net land | Net coverage | Comp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100k SF | rear-load, about 200 x 500 ft | about 7-9 ac | 26-33% | |
| 250k SF | rear-load, about 310 x 810 ft | about 15-18 ac | 32-38% | I-285 Logistics: 237,515 SF on about 17 ac = 32% |
| 500k SF | cross-dock, about 520 x 960 ft | about 30-38 ac | 30-38% | Parkway West: 571k SF on 45.8 ac gross = 28.6% |
| 1M SF | cross-dock, about 570 x 1,750 ft | about 50-65 ac net | | Oakley: 1.3M SF on 83 ac = 36%; national 60-90 ac gross |

Gross coverage on encumbered Fulton greenfield is far lower: 17-20% at Palmetto, 20.5% at Union City Commerce Center. So always report BOTH net and gross FAR.
Screening target: 0.35-0.45 net FAR for distribution; flag anything below 0.25 or above 0.50 net.

3) DOORS, TRAILERS, CARS
Doors per dock wall = floor((L - 2 x endClr 60 ft) / 12 ft). Report SF per door.
- Comps: cross-dock 3,460-4,780 SF/door; rear-load 5,700-6,000.
- ULI: about 3,500 SF/door for cross-dock, about 10,000 average; ARC: 5,000-15,000.
- Cap doors at a target ratio if desired. Spec developers place the maximum (TestFit default).

Trailer stalls = geometric count along the court edge and extra rows. Report stalls per door.
- Target at least 1.0 (Cushman: tenants want at least 1 extra per door).
- Local comps 1.0-1.45 per door; per-SF 1 per 3,400-5,800 SF.

Car stalls:
- Required = jurisdiction ratio x SF. Use zoning_rules.json when verified; South Fulton staff apply 1 per 1,000 SF; Union City uses 1 per employee + 1 per company vehicle; City of Atlanta required about 1.75 per 1,000 at I-285 Logistics.
- Provided = geometric count in employee lots on the office/non-dock sides.
- Market provides 0.3-0.7 per 1,000 for cross-dock bulk and 0.65-1.0 for 200-300k rear-load.
- Flag "parking variance likely" when the code requirement exceeds what fits. Report required vs provided, as TestFit does.

4) CIRCULATION AND ACCESS (currently missing; it is about 10-20% of paving)
- Perimeter truck drive: 30 ft two-way (prototype road.truck.width) from the truck entrance to each court. Car drive 24 ft.
- Fire: every exterior wall within reach of a 20 ft fire lane. Because all 32-40 ft clear boxes exceed 30 ft, draw a 26 ft aerial access lane 15-30 ft off one full long side; car lots and courts can double as it if unobstructed. A dead end over 150 ft needs a turnaround.
- Access points:
  - over 124k SF sprinklered (62k unsprinklered): 2 separate fire access roads, so draw at least 2 driveways;
  - truck and car driveways separate where frontage allows (ARC). Comps all show 2 driveways for 1M+ SF campuses; Union City Commerce Center shows 1 full-movement plus a secondary;
  - truck driveway curb radius 75 ft;
  - space driveways at least about 100 ft from intersections (NJ draft) and respect GDOT spacing on state routes;
  - driveway throat before any gate or guard house sized for 2-3 WB-67s, about 150-225 ft;
  - guard house optional, drawn as a small pad at the truck entrance only when the court is secured.
- Employee entrances at office corners next to car lots, with no pedestrian crossing of truck courts.
- Outdoor amenity: a small patio (about 1,000-2,500 SF) at office pods. Cosmetic; no source found for a standard size.

5) IMPERVIOUS, DETENTION, OPEN SPACE
Impervious = building + courts + trailer stalls + car lots + drives + walks.
- Sanity check: impervious / building footprint ≈ 2.0 (range 1.8-2.3) for bulk cross-dock in Fulton DRIs. Net impervious 70-80% (TR-55 industrial default 72%; Oakley 75-80%). Gross impervious 36-55% on encumbered sites.
- Replace the fixed pond with one sized from impervious area (see the detention topic). Interim placeholder: reserve 8-15% of net developable area, at the low point and outside stream buffers. The Midwest rule of 15-20% is a ceiling, not a Georgia default.
- Landscape/open = remainder. Report its %.

6) WHAT THE SCREEN SHOULD DRAW AND REPORT (to be credible to a developer)
Draw: parcel; net developable line (setbacks, buffers, floodplain); building with dock walls and office pods; truck courts with apron; trailer rows; car lots; truck and car drives; fire/aerial lanes; driveways with radii; optional gate; detention pond(s); open space.

Site data table:
- gross ac; net ac; building SF and L x W; configuration; clear height (prototype);
- FAR gross and net;
- dock doors and SF/door;
- trailer stalls and per door;
- car stalls required/provided and per 1,000;
- truck court depth;
- impervious ac and % (gross and net);
- detention ac and %; open space %;
- access points: count, truck vs car, fronting road;
- flags: fire two-road rule, aerial lane, parking variance, buffer encroachment, court-in-setback;
- list of assumptions.

Finally, check each ratio against the comp bands above and print a warning when outside.

Both should be confirmed from the adopted ordinances and recorded in zoning_rules.json.

verification.summary:
I checked all 35 findings against their sources. I downloaded the PDFs and searched the extracted text, and read the web pages with WebFetch. No CoStar, Crexi or Showcase pages were used. One LoopNet page was opened by mistake while looking for a mirror of the Cushman blog. It returned 403 and nothing from it was used.

Result: 26 confirmed, 8 corrected, 1 unsupported.

Corrections:
(1) Oakley DRI 2452: the DRI form says 75% impervious, not 80%. The 80% is only ARC's water-quality loading assumption, which treated the site as heavy industrial. The traffic narrative also lists 200 employee spaces, against 364 on the site plan.
(2) Derived impervious multiple: Core5 impervious is 50.7 ac (35.8% of 141.62 ac), not 50.5. Building cover plus open space sums to 100% in the DRI tables, which confirms that impervious includes the roofs.
(3) ARC truck stall row: the 53-60 ft trailer drop-stall figure credited to Innowave is not on the Innowave page.
(4) Innowave truck court row: the stall size of 12-14 ft x 53-60 ft is not on that page. The "1 per door, increasingly 2" claim comes from Innowave's separate Acre Test page.
(5) TestFit 3.14 page: it supports only three things. Trailer stalls can be computed from SF instead of dock doors. Access points are placed by the user with width and turning radius. Ring roads can be turned off. The car-per-1,000 setting, the max-dock default, the presets, the site table and the Prologis mention are all unsupported.
(6) Bisnow: it gives only Minooka, 1M SF on 69 ac (about 33%). The Dallas and Ocala comps are not in the article.
(7) Fire access road count row: Georgia applicability tightened. Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 120-3-3-.04 adopts the 2018 IFC, and its rewritten 503.1.1 requires compliance with Appendix D. Georgia also adds 504.1.1, about one exterior access door per 100 linear feet of wall.
(8) ARC truck court row: added a missed design item. Guidance calls for one 10x80 ft (12x80 preferred) truck staging space per two loading docks.

Unsupported: the Cushman blog (blog.cushwake.com) does not resolve in this session's network, and archive.org is blocked. A search snippet suggests a 2019 Cushman article said under 300 ft for single-load, but the 500-660 ft cross-dock range could not be confirmed.

Other notes:
- Most comps match their sources exactly.
- 5395 Oakley (Southpark) is an existing 2001 building. The page also lists 50 docks and 16 car spaces.
- In the Union City Commerce Center DRI, the 18.29 ac tract is being donated to the school system.
- In Palmetto, transportation stream crossings are allowed by ordinance. In Union City, an access-drive buffer intrusion needs a variance.
- South Fulton staff recommended denial of Z22-013. Its 100 ft stream buffer and 100 ft rear setback were the subject of variance requests.

Buildings over 30 ft or 3 stories need at least two means of fire apparatus access (D104.1). Georgia applicability: the Safety Fire Commissioner's rule, Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 120-3-3-.04, adopts the 2018 IFC with Georgia modifications. Its rewritten 503.1.1 requires access roads to comply with 'this section and Appendix D of this Code', so Appendix D applies to facilities under that rule, administered by the local fire official. Georgia adds D107.2: where two roads are required, they must be separated by at least half the property's overall diagonal. It also adds 504.1.1, generally one exterior access door per 100 linear feet of wall, adjustable by local officials. Confirm the current edition and local amendments with the Fulton County, city or state fire official.
